item.text: This is a small flat Java project with no build file and a clean worktree. I’m reading the model classes now to find duplication or fragile logic worth tightening without changing the simulation behavior.

The main duplication is around movement eligibility and food selection; the same terrain predicate appears in multiple places, and `findFood` loops over the prey map in a way that does redundant work. I’m checking subclasses before editing so constructor/birth patterns stay intact.

I found a contained refactor target: centralize “can this actor occupy this location” in `Field`, then use it from movement and population. That removes duplicated terrain checks and makes future water/land rules less error-prone.

I’m going to edit `Field`, `Animal`, `Actor`, `Simulator`, and a few raw generic initializers. The behavior should remain the same; the main change is moving terrain eligibility into one method and simplifying repeated lookups.
The first refactor pass is in place. I’m compiling now to catch type or access issues before doing any cleanup.
